changes.place: Opening fourth line, after donne lieu
changes.scan_shows: The enlarged mark consists of a short narrow upper stroke and a detached lower diamond-like point. There is no visible a loop or connecting baseline stroke. The C doubt is resolved as a colon.

Settled in half_a: the brace lies above H²(E′(M,N)), and P(M,N) lies above the brace. The region below the term does not contain the label. The stated approximate box is in the whole-source coordinates.
A long horizontal upper stroke connects to a downward left loop with a short returning inner stroke. This is the sigma form, rather than the two curves of a Latin s. C uncertainty removed.

changes.place: Heuristiquement, second argument of E prime: possible underlying layer
changes.scan_shows: Several heavy angular strokes overlap in the second argument. An earlier M or N cannot be isolated confidently from the retracing. I retain these candidates and add a no-independent-underletter alternative; the phantom does not deny the visible heavy strokes.

changes.place: Heuristiquement, second argument of E prime: live alphabet
changes.scan_shows: The visible form has two thick side strokes and a diagonal, but their breadth and internal gaps do not securely distinguish ordinary N retraced during correction from a deliberately doubled N. C live-alphabet doubt retained exactly.
Settled in half_a: two short high pen strokes stand before 2-champ; there are no angled guillemet strokes. This compares literal punctuation, not a macro-name conversion.

changes.place: Immediately after strict in the first quoted expression
changes.scan_shows: The crop shows exactly one pair of high closing strokes immediately after strict. It does not show a second closing quotation layer or a separate guillemet.

changes.h: « épinglés » par M, N; editorial note explicitly credits the insertion
changes.scan_shows: The dotted i is followed by a separate horizontal dash without an n arch. The later g has a descending return stroke distinct from the insertion connector. Both quotation boundaries are paired high strokes. The connector attaches the entire phrase after the closing stricts parenthesis and before sur. H already records the inserted state; the disagreement is the word and quotation form.

Settled in half_b: the first character of ta has a short ascending stem crossed near its lower part; the following low a is separate from the tall initial stroke of théorie. It is t, not the looped l of la.
The crop resolves the initial co, the two separate r-like shoulders, the low e/s group, the long p descender, a small o, and the n-d ending. C single-candidate doubt removed.

changes.place: Underline in final Picard stricts phrase
changes.scan_shows: The underline starts beneath the r/i junction and runs under the middle ict region, ending at the final t stem. It does not extend under the initial st or the terminal s. I retain C’s closest letter-span representation.

A separate horizontal dash again follows the dotted i. There is no rising n shoulder. The long lower return is continuous with the g descender and is not a separate underline. This also resolves the recurrence covered by C alerts.

The final glyph of the first word is a long low horizontal stroke with a descending end, like the final s of cas in the same crop. It has no rising stem or crossing bar comparable to the final t in canoniquement.
The enlargement separates c-a, the low n-o-n group, the dotted i, the looped q with its long descender, and the u-e-m-e-n-t sequence. C single-candidate doubt removed.

changes.place: Quotation marks around à la main

A tall loop and small lower loops remain beneath a broad crossing/return stroke. The first letter may be l or d; no uncancelled replacement article is visible before terme. C doubt retained.

changes.scan_shows: An initial t has a clear transverse bar, followed by a low e/r group and the final m-e humps. C single-candidate doubt removed.

changes.place: Final line, noun before the correction

notes: Coverage: every text block and every inline and displayed formula was read line by line against BOTH C.tex and H.tex. Agreed words, endings, accents, punctuation, capital alphabets, primes, indices, exponents, underlines, braces, arrows, insertions and deletions were inspected. This is a visual coverage statement, not a mathematical proof check.

Workflow: the whole image was opened once for layout, half_a once, and half_b once, in that order. The 16 local crops were generated once each from the assigned whole source and opened once each. No whole/half was reopened, no settled locus was recropped, no other scan or reader return was opened, and no OCR or recognition software was used. Approximate source_box_approx coordinates in half-settled change rows refer to the original 1139×1739 whole image and are supplied for the main reader’s adjudication crops.

The page is entirely handwritten in an unnamed pen hand; no personal identity is independently established by this page packet. The archive 9 is in a lighter pencil hand. There is no visible new date, salutation, heading, signature, author page number, or total page count. The reading begins with donc and ends unfinished at près des.

The opening states that E′(M,N) is a complex whose underlined H^i invariants are those of E(M,N) in degree i+2, then writes a degree-2 exact sequence with middle term named P(M,N). This is an account of what the source says, not an independently established theorem.

The paragraph beginning Heuristiquement offers an interpretation by a 2-champ de Picard strict and explicitly assumes that the addressee’s theory for strict 1-champs extends to strict 2-champs. The tentative Heuristiquement, en admettant, and ce qui pour moi ne fait guère de doute remain in the reading.

The final paragraph states that the exact sequence is constructed canonically à la main and begins describing the middle sheaf up to équivalence. It contains a cancelled article, an uncertain noun, and a cancelled preposition replaced by a raised à. I transcribe the à at the hook’s attachment before the cancelled old glyph.

The exact sequence is a one-line display. There are no independent diagrams or non-diagram drawings on this page. The long connectors under the two interlinear additions and the final à hook are insertion marks, represented by inserted at their attachments, not separate figures.

All thirteen explicit C doubt loci are represented in changes, whether resolved or retained; the repeated épi-glés alert is also recorded. C’s additional mathematical alert rows were verified in the notation entries rather than being turned into no-change differences.

No mathematical proof, independent re-proof, formal computation, or use-and-recheck was performed in this reading. The source assertions and its heuristic qualification are documented above; math_checks is therefore empty.
No prose abbreviation requires expansion on this page. Ext and Hom are retained as mathematical operator names and recorded in notation.
